title: Kidney-injury models show changing laboratory contributions before recorded onset
summary: A reweighted XGBoost analysis of hospital records compared feature contributions at24,48 and72 hours before kidney-injury onset. Laboratory measurements accounted for54.5% of the model-score contrast increase from72 to24 hours. This describes learned-model attributions in one hospital, not the causal effect of changing those measurements.
organization: Jinan University; University of Kansas Medical Center

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, model evaluation and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Modified feature-sampling weights emphasize prespecified modifiable feature views; fitted models and SHAP-derived score contrasts quantify how learned associations differ by retrospective prediction window.
evidence.tested: The24-hour cohort contained144084 encounters; models trained on2010–2016 and tested on2017–2018. Cohort sizes differed for longer windows. Fifty random-seed repetitions informed mean attributions.
evidence.unknown: Feature views were deliberately reweighted, so their importance is conditional on that modeling choice. AKI cases were anchored to first onset, controls to last creatinine measurement; repeated encounters and different window cohorts limit comparisons. Correlations among modifiable factors were not modeled explicitly. The source’s predicted intervention benefits are not measured treatment effects, patient-specific causal risks or prevention evidence. Supplementary algorithm/hyperparameter details were not independently read.
